clue.text: Trouble involving Republican poet's fellowship

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: bother is trouble or fuss
R is the standard abbreviation for Republican
Thomas Hood, the nineteenth-century English poet

explanation.surface: A political row breaks out inside a literary society over a Republican poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s joins the poet to the definition and gives no letters. Thomas Hood is a favourite crossword poet, alongside Pope, Gray and Burns.
explanation.definitionFit: Brotherhood means a body of people joined in common purpose, the same sense as a fellowship or guild.

clue.text: A couple of females propping up bar in Scottish town

indicators.note: in a down entry, whatever props something up sits underneath it, so it is written after

parts.note: to bar is to ban or prohibit
F is the abbreviation for female, and a couple means two of them

explanation.surface: Two women lean on the bar of a pub in a small Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface bar is a pub counter; the wordplay needs the verb, to forbid. Banff is a small coastal town in Aberdeenshire, north-east Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Banff is a royal burgh on the Moray Firth coast, an actual settlement in northern Scotland.

clue.text: Negotiated about broken plate

parts.note: over can mean about, as in a dispute over money

indicators.note: a broken object is in pieces that can be put back together differently

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone haggled over the price of a broken dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Negotiated looks like bargaining, but here it means got past an obstacle, as a horse negotiates a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: To negotiate a hurdle is to get over it successfully, and overleapt means jumped clear over it.

clue.text: Hired assassin decapitated poet

indicators.note: losing the head means losing the first letter of the word

parts.note: Walt Whitman, the American poet of Leaves of Grass

explanation.surface: A contract killer has beheaded a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the W from the front of the poet's surname to leave the six letters, split three and three.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit man is a professional killer paid to murder a target, exactly what a hired assassin does.

clue.text: Rubbish right outside entrance to oratory

indicators.note: being outside something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: Rt is the abbreviation for right, as in Rt Hon

indicators.note: the entrance is where you come in, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of oratory; the reversed run inside the word is a coincidence

explanation.surface: Litter has piled up just outside the door of a chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: Right here is the two-letter abbreviation, not the single R, so it can be split around the O. An oratory is a small chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: Rot is informal speech for nonsense, a common synonym for rubbish in the sense of foolish talk.

clue.text: Reject not in group performing play

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
the cast is the company of actors in a play

explanation.surface: An actor dropped from the company cannot join the performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Reject looks like a verb but is the noun, a person cast aside.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast is someone rejected by society, so a reject in the noun sense of a person turned away.

clue.text: Rule broken by English knight in branch of church

indicators.note: something broken into is split open so another piece can sit inside it

parts.note: domination is rule or control
E is the abbreviation for English
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: An English knight defies the rules of his church.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess notation K is the king, so the knight is N.
explanation.definitionFit: A denomination is a distinct religious body within Christianity, such as Methodists or Baptists, a branch of the wider church.

clue.text: Complete control of admiral finally entering unfamiliar cargo area

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: strange means unfamiliar or new

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of admiral
a ship's hold is where cargo is stowed

explanation.surface: An admiral takes full charge of a ship by marching into a strange cargo deck.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter slips in just before the final E of the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stranglehold, literally a choking grip, is used figuratively for total domination over something.

clue.text: Function a northern group originally held in shelter

indicators.note: something held in is kept inside, so these letters sit within another word

parts.note: a tent is a simple shelter
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for northern

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of group

explanation.surface: A gathering of northern people sheltering together.
explanation.walkthrough: Function looks like an event or a purpose, but it is the mathematical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangent is one of the trigonometric functions, alongside sine and cosine, so it is a mathematical example.

clue.text: Giant bird primarily attacking nestlings

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letters are kept

parts.note: the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A huge bird swoops on chicks in their nest.
explanation.walkthrough: Primarily applies to both words that follow, taking one opening letter from each.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were the gigantic gods of Greek myth, so the word now names any person or thing of huge size or power.

clue.text: A fat file I arranged to band together

indicators.note: arranging things puts them into a new order

parts.note: all nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone organises a thick dossier so that a group can unite.
explanation.walkthrough: Band reads like a musical group, but here it is a verb meaning to join up.
explanation.definitionFit: To affiliate is to join or associate officially with an organisation, so to unite or ally with others.

clue.text: Doctor copies friend of bishop

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, altering its form

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A doctor duplicates documents for a bishop's companion.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor looks like a person, but it is a verb telling you to alter the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Episcopal is the adjective relating to bishops, from the Greek episkopos, overseer.

clue.text: End of a motorway going west

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in an across entry, travelling west means reading right to left

parts.note: the M1, Britain's first long motorway, written with I for 1

explanation.surface: The far end of a motorway heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the main motorway north from London; setters write the 1 as letter I. Only that piece turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: An end can mean a goal or purpose, as in 'to that end', which is what an aim is.

clue.text: Easy-going girl touring eastern part of UK

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: gal is an informal word for girl
E is the abbreviation for eastern
NI is Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A relaxed young woman is on holiday in the east of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: Eastern part of UK looks like East Anglia, but it splits into two pieces: the E and Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Genial means friendly and cheerful in manner, close to relaxed and easy-going.

clue.text: Directions restricting a girl's nursemaids

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so outer pieces confine an inner one

parts.note: N and S are the compass points north and south
Annie is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl's carers are given strict rules about what she may do.
explanation.walkthrough: The two compass letters bracket the name; the apostrophe-s simply joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nannies are women employed to look after children, the modern term for nursemaids.

clue.text: In Kent, oddly, it's a young animal

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so these letters come out in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a creature in Kent is, strangely, just a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: Oddly usually means take the odd letters, but here it is an anagram signal. Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitten is the young of a cat, so a specific example of a young animal.

clue.text: Possibly Irving's capital?

parts.note: surface reading: whatever money or wealth a man called Irving owns
setter's reading: a capital city that shares its name with the songwriter Irving

explanation.walkthrough: Capital suggests money, but it is a capital city sharing the surname of the songwriter of White Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: The German capital shares its name with Irving Berlin, so in a whimsical sense it belongs to him.

clue.text: A long time in Berkshire college — wasting time!

indicators.note: to waste something is to lose it, so a letter drops out

parts.note: Eton College is the famous school in Berkshire
T is the abbreviation for time, the letter removed

explanation.surface: Pupils spend ages at an English boarding school, frittering hours away.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is the elite boarding school near Windsor in Berkshire, a county west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is an immensely long period, used loosely for any age or very lengthy stretch.

clue.text: Acerbic worker, say, beside dyke

indicators.note: beside means next to, so one piece sits right after another

parts.note: a dyke can be a ditch or channel, a trench
the worker ant is a classic example of a worker

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued labourer stands by a drainage ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: Worker is a crossword staple for the insect; 'say' shows it is an example. A dyke in British use can be a ditch as well as an embankment.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant means vigorously incisive and cutting, as acerbic remarks are sharp and biting.

clue.text: A western fellow — bristly

parts.note: taken as written
W is the abbreviation for western
Ned is a man's name, so a fellow

explanation.surface: A cowboy from a western film turns out to be a prickly character.
explanation.walkthrough: Western suggests a cowboy film, but it gives only its abbreviation letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Awns are the stiff hairs on ears of barley and other grasses, so awned plants are covered in such spikes.

clue.text: Outstanding old air force formation

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a wing is a unit of an air force

explanation.surface: Praise for a superb display by a veteran squadron.
explanation.walkthrough: Outstanding sounds like praise, but it means still unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is outstanding has not yet been paid, so the money is still owing.

clue.text: Set up newspaper? Something fishy here

indicators.note: in a down entry, setting up means lifting so the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone smells a rat over the launch of a new newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Something fishy suggests a suspicious scheme, but it literally means a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The gar, or garfish, is a long slender fish with a needle-like snout, so it is literally fishy.

clue.text: Slowly father enters Greek port

indicators.note: whatever enters goes inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: lento is the musical direction for slowly
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Dad makes a leisurely arrival at a harbour in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: Lento is Italian for slow, a tempo marking in music. Lepanto, now Nafpaktos, gave its name to the 1571 naval battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lepanto is the historic name of a harbour town on the Gulf of Corinth, so a port in Greece.

clue.text: Brassed off retired man made noise like pig crossing lake

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Sid is a man's name

indicators.note: crossing means going across, so one piece spans another

parts.note: a pig grunts
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A fed-up pensioner snorted like a pig as he walked past a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Brassed off is British slang for fed up. Retired looks like a pensioner, but it tells you to turn the name back.
explanation.definitionFit: Disgruntled means annoyed and dissatisfied, the same feeling as British slang for being fed up.
